title: Flex Commit Lanes and Scope Decomposition Playbook for Cycle Planning
creator: Evelyn Ross
description: Playbook to allocate flexible committed lanes (core, stretch, reserve) and a repeatable scope-decomposition process so PMs can size initiatives consistently across infra, runtime, console, and product-org dependencies. Aims to reduce cycle overcommit by 25% and increase predictability for Dedicated and Private launch milestones.
acceptance_criteria: A standard 3-lane template (Core / Stretch / Reserve) is added to the cycle planning doc and used by 100% of product initiatives for 2026-Q2 planning.
Backlog grooming checklist updated with decomposition steps and engineering input at triage.
Two pilot initiatives use the playbook and report estimated vs delivered velocity variance <15%.
SLA for Dedicated capacity tickets included as dependency tracking on the initiative page.
A dashboard card in Roadmap Console shows committed vs flexible capacity per cycle.
Hand-off checklist to Solutions Eng and SEs for Private deployments is included in the template.
deliverables: Cycle planning playbook doc (Confluence) with lane definitions and sample decompositions
Template Linear issue checklist and labels for lane assignment
Engineer+PM decomposition workshop materials and recording
Roadmap Console dashboard card spec and initial mock
Two pilot initiative retros with before/after velocity metrics
timeline: Week 1: Draft playbook and templates; Week 2: Host 2 cross-functional decomposition workshops (ENG, RE, DS, SRE); Week 3: Run pilot on Runtime-1.20 and Console-UX initiatives; Week 4: Collect metrics, iterate, and publish final playbook.
risks: Under-estimation from infra-dependent work (Dedicated/Private) leading to reserve depletion
Teams may default to marking items as Core to guarantee staffing, reducing effectiveness
Dashboard implementation delays if data model for committed capacity is not ready
Cross-team dependencies (SRE, Platform) may not be available for decomposition sessions on schedule
decisions: Three-lane model selected (Core 60%, Stretch 25%, Reserve 15% by default) — adjustable per org after baseline runs
Engineering estimates will be required at Triage for any item >5 points to be classified Core
Reserve capacity can be reallocated 1x per cycle during a sanctioned mid-cycle replan with VP approval
Owners: PMs own lane assignment; Eng leads sign-off on Core acceptability; Solutions Eng owns Private/Dedicated readiness checklist
tradeoffs: Higher default Core allocation increases predictability but reduces exploratory work and long-term R&D capacity
Larger Reserve improves risk mitigation but can encourage conservative planning and artificially low scope commitments
Requiring estimates at triage increases planning overhead but reduces downstream rework and fire-drill incidents
